note: v1: NOBODY PLAYS THE BASS, deep heavy house in F# minor, 120 rising to 120.5, built on THE MISSING FUNDAMENTAL. The bass line is played by nobody: only its 2nd to 6th harmonics sound (phantom-bass; measured, its fundamentals sit 14 dB under its harmonics) and the ear supplies the low note. The seam with t5 is the illusion: t6 comes in with a phantom F# under t5's real 808 on F#1, so as the crossfade takes the real sub away the bass goes on being heard. Through the deeper section the line drops an octave, to notes no club speaker plays. In the break the bass is taken apart: five exact partials (2 to 6 times F#1, a new 'partial' patch, ratios checked by FFT) enter one by one, staggered and spread across the field so you hear a bright chord, then gather to the centre and start pulsing in one rhythm until they fuse and the low F# appears; the drop brings the real sub at last (and loses it for two bars at 127-128, while the bass stays). The stair (F# G# A C#) is climbed by the bass nobody plays at the end of the groove and of the drop; the outro takes the real sub away and settles the phantom on C# for t7. Congas, a dark minor-ninth pad on a seven-bar filter LFO, stabs on the 'e' of one and the 'a' of three into a 3/8 dub delay. Mix: the machine-kit kick masked the phantom line by 14 dB (solos measured), so it sits 7 dB lower; a master tilt (-6 dB under 220 Hz, +3 over 4 kHz) keeps the harmonics' shape. Loudness -11 (TP -1.28, runs 2); seeds 0/11 84.88 / 84.85; spectrum 58 and the t5 seam (flow 40: t5's last bars are near-silent; fixing in t5) are next.
next: t5's ending (kick to the last bar for the seam), then t6's spectrum (58) and structure (6 sections).

note: v2: THE LINE KEEPS CHANGING, ITS COLOUR MOVES, AND THE HOLE. The phantom bass played one roll every bar; now four figures rotate every eight bars (the roll, pushed sixteenths, an octave leap, and a half-time figure that opens the second drop). A band-pass on the phantom line sweeps across its harmonics on an eleven-bar LFO, favouring the 2nd and then the 6th: the bass's colour turns from round to nasal while its PITCH never moves - the ear takes pitch from the whole harmonic series, not from any one harmonic: the other half of the missing-fundamental story. THE HOLE (bars 65-68): in the deeper section, where the line has dropped below what speakers play, the drums vanish for four bars and the bass nobody plays is left alone, until a rising hat roll brings the kit back. The drop is now two: the pad and congas leave for the second, the stabs move to every off-beat, the bass goes half-time and then leaps. And the pad moved up an octave, out of the bass's harmonics (A2-G#3 sat right on the 83-292 Hz excess). Seeds 0/11 (v1 85.39 / 85.36 rescored): 86.47 / 86.44, now stable across seeds (structure finds 7 sections, 98.6; v2 without the hole split seeds 74/87); spectrum 58 -> 70, cohesion 57 -> 72; levels clean (-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.28, runs 2).

note: v3: THE GHOST OF THE BASS, and the stair in chirper-two's voice. In both drops the phantom line's accented notes are echoed three octaves up on celesta, a sixteenth late, into the 3/8 dub delay: the melody you've been hearing in the bass that isn't there, spelled out high where it can't be missed (and filling the 1-3 kHz presence the track lacked). THE STAIR, which the phantom bass climbs at the end of the groove and of the second drop, is now doubled by chirper-two's c2-stair (borrowed with credit: a Shepard tone under a fixed 600 Hz bell) counting on: the bass that isn't there and a tone that never gets higher climbing together. And the hats now run from bar 1, matching t5's tail through the overlap.
